REVOBOTS

 PUBLIC KNOWLEDGE BASE / VERSION 1.0

 Non-confidential public-facing reference | Prepared 2026-10-09 | Editorial review copy


 Purpose

 A source-linked content library for a REVOBOTS conversational AI assistant. Built for easy maintenance and retrieval,
 including CES preparation and broader TASKBOT use cases.

 Editorial standards

 • Use only public, approved facts and clearly separate historical accomplishments, tested deployments, proposed
 capabilities, and future plans.

 • Maintain a confident, forward-looking voice without inventing claims or guaranteeing performance.

 • Never use the knowledge base as a substitute for application-level guardrails, moderation, or access controls.

 • Exclude private people and employment information, financial details, confidential customer matters, internal
 discussions, and unannounced projects.

 • When sources are insufficient, decline speculation and offer the official REVOBOTS site or a representative.

 Source limitations

 The linked Notion nomenclature glossary could not be retrieved publicly. A private draft one-pager was not used as proof
 of publication. Pending terms are listed separately as editorial-review items and are excluded from the ingestion-ready
 JSONL.

 Records ready for source-based retrieval: 47. Editorial items on hold: 5.

 COMPANY

 Mission and future of work

 Quick answer: REVOBOTS aims to help people focus on valuable work by assigning repetitive, demanding, or difficult
 tasks to appropriately designed robotic systems.

 The company presents robotics as a complement to human capability. In official messaging, human-robot collaboration,
 rapid iteration, safety-minded oversight, and usefulness in everyday operations are recurring themes.

 ID: company-mission | Terms: mission, purpose, future of work

 Source(s): https://revobots.ai/ | https://revobots.ai/mwc25 | https://revobots.ai/ces2026

 The four Ds of physical work

 Quick answer: REVOBOTS highlights Dangerous, Dexterous, Dirty, and Dull work as areas where task-adaptive robotics
 can help.

 These categories are descriptive, not a promise that any robot can execute every task. Specific use cases are scoped to
 their environment, payload, perception, safety, and operating constraints.




REVOBOTS INC  |  Public Knowledge Base v1.0  |  REVIEW DRAFT                                                                                      1

ID: four-ds | Terms: dangerous dirty dull dexterous, 4Ds, four D work

 Source(s): https://revobots.ai/ces2026 | https://www.linkedin.com/company/revobots/

 What is REVOBOTS?

 Quick answer: REVOBOTS develops task-adaptive, AI-enabled robotic systems designed around real work in
 human-centered environments.

 REVOBOTS focuses on practical Physical AI: matching the robot, its software, and the level of human oversight to the
 task. Its public communications emphasize configurable robotic hardware, direct digital manufacturing, and deployments
 intended to support people as organizations address labor-intensive work.

 ID: company-overview | Terms: about revobots, what does revobots do, REVOBOTS INC

 Source(s): https://revobots.ai/ | https://revobots.ai/ces2026 | https://www.linkedin.com/company/revobots/

 BRAND

 BOTS ON!

 Quick answer: BOTS ON! is REVOBOTS’ public rallying cry.

 It appears in REVOBOTS company messaging to convey execution, optimism, and momentum. Use sparingly and
 naturally, not after every answer.

 ID: bots-on | Terms: BOTS ON, rally cry

 Source(s): https://revobots.ai/ | https://in.linkedin.com/company/revobots

 REVOBOTS mission statement and slogan

 Quick answer: REVOBOTS uses the line “We build robots that work like people—so people don’t have to work like
 robots.”

 This line emphasizes designing robotics to carry out useful work while preserving human attention for judgment,
 creativity, relationships, and higher-value responsibilities. Preserve the official intent when paraphrasing.

 ID: company-tagline | Terms: we build robots that work like people, tagline, slogan

 Source(s): https://revobots.ai/

 TECHNOLOGY

 Autonomy with human oversight

 Quick answer: REVOBOTS combines autonomous operation with human-in-the-loop oversight when circumstances
 require it.

 REVOBOTS describes an operating model in which a robot can handle defined workflows while remote or local people
 train, supervise, and intervene as needed. Human oversight is a design principle, not a guarantee that every
 circumstance can be automated.

 ID: automation-safety | Terms: human-in-the-loop, HITL, operator oversight

 Source(s): https://revobots.ai/mwc25 | https://revobots.ai/scoutxt | https://revobots.ai/ces2026

 Human-centered automation

 Quick answer: REVOBOTS designs automation to work alongside people and to preserve the role of human supervision
 where appropriate.







REVOBOTS INC  |  Public Knowledge Base v1.0  |  REVIEW DRAFT                                                                                            2

A core public message is that robotics can reduce routine physical burden and give teams more capacity for roles
 requiring decision-making, service, and expertise. Avoid framing the company as seeking to displace people wholesale.

 ID: human-centered | Terms: human plus robot, humans+robots, collaborative robotics

 Source(s): https://revobots.ai/mwc25 | https://revobots.ai/ces2026 | https://revobots.ai/scoutxt

 Modular TASKBOT configuration

 Quick answer: TASKBOT systems can be configured with different tools, sensors, manipulators, and mobility options.

 The specific physical embodiment follows the task: a robot might need a mobile base, arm and gripper, or a different
 form factor. Public company materials stress practical modularity, not a universal hardware template.

 ID: robot-modularity | Terms: modular robots, end-effectors, custom taskbot

 Source(s): https://revobots.ai/mwc25 | https://revobots.ai/ | https://revobots.ai/press

 Physical AI

 Quick answer: Physical AI connects intelligent software with machines that sense and act in the physical world.

 In REVOBOTS public messaging, Physical AI brings robotic motion, perception, autonomy, and human supervision into
 practical workflows. The focus is not only generating information but helping perform physical tasks reliably.

 ID: physical-ai | Terms: embodied AI, embodied intelligence, robot intelligence

 Source(s): https://revobots.ai/ces2026 | https://revobots.ai/ | https://www.linkedin.com/posts/revobots_revobots-pwcs-emtechexchange-2026-activit
 y-7440370244927455232-28hc

 REVO PILOT

 Quick answer: REVO PILOT is REVOBOTS’ name for its human-in-the-loop support and supervision approach.

 Public materials associate REVO PILOT with remote operator guidance, task learning, and escalation for supervision
 when autonomy needs assistance.

 ID: revo-pilot | Terms: REVO Pilot, REVO PILOTS, robot pilot, human pilot

 Source(s): https://revobots.ai/ | https://revobots.ai/scoutxt | https://revobots.ai/mwc25

 Rapid prototyping and direct digital manufacturing

 Quick answer: REVOBOTS uses modular design and 3D printing to adapt robotic systems to different tasks.

 Direct digital manufacturing can support faster physical iteration and task-specific components. Public materials describe
 modular hardware, different mobility configurations, sensors, and interchangeable tools. Precise manufacturing
 specifications depend on the product.

 ID: innovation-approach | Terms: 3d printed robotics, DDM, direct digital manufacturing

 Source(s): https://revobots.ai/mwc25 | https://revobots.ai/

 Task-adaptive robotics

 Quick answer: Task-adaptive robotics starts with the job to be done and selects the robotic configuration around that job.

 Instead of treating one robot shape as the answer to every problem, REVOBOTS emphasizes selecting mobility,
 manipulators, cameras, sensors, tools, and intelligence that fit specific workflows. This can include mobile and
 humanoid-inspired designs; humanoid appearance is not a universal requirement.

 ID: task-adaptive | Terms: purpose-built robotics, task-specific robotics, task adaptive

 Source(s): https://revobots.ai/ces2026 | https://revobots.ai/mwc25 | https://revobots.ai/








REVOBOTS INC  |  Public Knowledge Base v1.0  |  REVIEW DRAFT                                                                                                 3

What autonomy means in practice

 Quick answer: Robot autonomy is evaluated against a defined task, environment, and operating constraints.

 REVOBOTS describes autonomy supported by perception, AI-driven control, and human oversight. Real-world behavior
 and deployment readiness depend on the tested configuration; capabilities should never be generalized beyond the
 supported use case.

 ID: rai-limits | Terms: fully autonomous, autonomous robotics, what can robots do

 Source(s): https://revobots.ai/ces2026 | https://revobots.ai/scoutxt

 PRODUCTS

 REVOLAB and microfactory concept

 Quick answer: REVOLAB describes REVOBOTS’ distributed, modular robotic manufacturing concept.

 The corporate website describes deployable microfactories and the concept of robots helping build robots. Treat the
 microfactory narrative as a company vision and program concept, not proof of a particular production facility or location.

 ID: revolab-public | Terms: REVO LAB, REVO LABS, REVOLABS, microfactory, robot builds robot

 Source(s): https://revobots.ai/

 TASKBOT AVA

 Quick answer: TASKBOT AVA is REVOBOTS’ humanoid-inspired task-adaptive robotic platform.

 REVOBOTS described AVA publicly in its CES 2026 release as a platform for jobs where human-scale reach, interaction,
 or versatility may be useful. That does not mean all TASKBOTS are humanoids.

 ID: taskbot-ava | Terms: AVA, Adaptive Vocational Avatar, humanoid taskbot

 Source(s): https://revobots.ai/ces2026 | https://revobots.ai/

 TASKBOT PORTER

 Quick answer: TASKBOT PORTER is a mobile manipulation platform designed around picking, moving, retrieving, and
 delivering objects.

 REVOBOTS announced TASKBOT PORTER in May 2026. Later official REVOBOTS coverage of Ellucian Live 2026
 previewed its one-arm multifunction concept. Describe applications such as material movement as intended use cases
 unless a specific production deployment is publicly verified.

 ID: taskbot-porter | Terms: PORTER, porter robot, fetch and carry robot

 Source(s): https://revobots.ai/taskbotporter | https://www.linkedin.com/posts/revobots_ellucian-live-2026-recap-activity-7453099120279330816-ITg
 A | https://in.linkedin.com/company/revobots

 TASKBOT SCOUT

 Quick answer: TASKBOT SCOUT is a mobile robotic platform for patrol, enforcement, safety-oriented presence, and
 inspection workflows.

 REVOBOTS describes TASKBOT SCOUT for activities such as parking oversight, compliance checks, security patrols,
 escorts, and inventory monitoring. Actual enabled duties depend on deployment-specific setup and applicable policies.

 ID: taskbot-scout | Terms: SCOUT, scout robot, campus scout

 Source(s): https://revobots.ai/ | https://revobots.ai/ces2026 | https://revobots.ai/scoutxt

 TASKBOT SCOUT XT

 Quick answer: TASKBOT SCOUT XT adapts the SCOUT platform for outdoor environments and variable terrain.




REVOBOTS INC  |  Public Knowledge Base v1.0  |  REVIEW DRAFT                                                                                            4

The March 2026 company announcement describes an IP65-rated enclosure, extended-wheelbase mobility,
 all-wheel-drive design, and upgraded outdoor sensing/navigation. Its platform is intended for use on changing surfaces
 and in outdoor campus operations.

 ID: taskbot-scout-xt | Terms: SCOUT XT, outdoor scout, all terrain scout

 Source(s): https://revobots.ai/scoutxt

 TASKBOT product family

 Quick answer: TASKBOT is the family name for REVOBOTS’ task-adaptive robots.

 Product references use the TASKBOT family name at first mention—such as TASKBOT SCOUT, TASKBOT SCOUT XT,
 TASKBOT PORTER, and TASKBOT AVA. Individual systems are developed around different operational tasks and settings.

 ID: taskbot-family | Terms: TASKBOTS, taskbot, robot family

 Source(s): https://revobots.ai/ | https://revobots.ai/ces2026 | https://revobots.ai/taskbotporter | https://revobots.ai/scoutxt

 USE CASES

 Campus operations

 Quick answer: Higher education is a documented setting for REVOBOTS’ TASKBOT SCOUT and SCOUT XT.

 Official announcements describe campus patrol and parking-compliance support, with human teams retaining
 responsibility for oversight and operations. REVOBOTS has publicly discussed collaboration with Campus Innovation and
 institutions including Xavier University and Indiana Wesleyan University.

 ID: campus | Terms: higher education, university robots, campus robots

 Source(s): https://revobots.ai/ces2026 | https://revobots.ai/scoutxt | https://in.linkedin.com/company/revobots

 Logistics and warehousing

 Quick answer: REVOBOTS designs robotics concepts for defined material handling and logistics workflows.

 Use cases can involve retrieval, transport, and placement, depending on the robot configuration. The company’s
 philosophy is to customize the physical and AI stack to the environment rather than promise every payload or reach.

 ID: logistics | Terms: warehouse, fulfillment, inventory movement

 Source(s): https://revobots.ai/mwc25 | https://revobots.ai/taskbotporter | https://revobots.ai/ces2026

 Manufacturing automation

 Quick answer: REVOBOTS targets repetitive and labor-intensive physical workflows that benefit from task-specific
 automation.

 Manufacturing concepts may include machine-side assistance, component movement, inspection, and other clearly
 scoped tasks. Feasibility must be validated for each workflow and environment.

 ID: manufacturing | Terms: factory, industrial automation, production robotics

 Source(s): https://revobots.ai/mwc25 | https://revobots.ai/ces2026 | https://revobots.ai/

 Parking enforcement support

 Quick answer: TASKBOT SCOUT platforms have been publicly described supporting parking patrol and compliance
 workflows.

 The SCOUT XT announcement references automatic license-plate recognition pilot activity at Xavier. Actual policies and
 enforcement decisions remain subject to each operator’s procedures. Avoid asserting universal citation rates or financial
 results.




REVOBOTS INC  |  Public Knowledge Base v1.0  |  REVIEW DRAFT                                                                                             5

ID: parking | Terms: ALPR, license plate recognition, parking robot

 Source(s): https://revobots.ai/scoutxt | https://revobots.ai/ces2026

 Patrol and inspection

 Quick answer: REVOBOTS’ mobile systems are designed for recurring patrol, observation, and inspection tasks.

 Public materials mention on-site inspection, security-oriented presence, and compliance monitoring. Availability of
 particular features depends on deployment-specific configuration and the organization’s requirements.

 ID: inspection | Terms: security patrol, routine inspection, monitoring

 Source(s): https://revobots.ai/ | https://revobots.ai/ces2026

 Retail and service environments

 Quick answer: REVOBOTS sees retail and service settings as potential applications for task-adaptive robotics.

 Public product concepts include moving objects and supporting routine physical work. Each project requires assessment
 of the items, work area, safety requirements, and required interactions; a retail concept is not automatically a deployed
 retail solution.

 ID: retail | Terms: retail robotics, hospitality robots, service robotics

 Source(s): https://revobots.ai/mwc25 | https://revobots.ai/taskbotporter | https://revobots.ai/ces2026

 PUBLIC ENGAGEMENTS

 Campus Innovation collaboration

 Quick answer: REVOBOTS has publicly identified Campus Innovation as a collaborator on university campus operations.

 Official public releases associate Campus Innovation with SCOUT and SCOUT XT campus deployments and C-Park-related
 workflows. Discuss only the publicly described collaboration, not private commercial arrangements.

 ID: campus-innovation | Terms: Campus Innovation, C-Park

 Source(s): https://revobots.ai/ces2026 | https://revobots.ai/scoutxt | https://in.linkedin.com/company/revobots

 Indiana Wesleyan University

 Quick answer: REVOBOTS publicly congratulated Indiana Wesleyan University on welcoming TASKBOT SCOUT XT into
 campus safety operations.

 The official REVOBOTS LinkedIn company update describes SCOUT XT supporting the campus police team with
 parking-lot patrols. This is a public account of adoption; do not add unpublished delivery milestones, project scope, or
 contractual details.

 ID: iwu | Terms: IWU, Indiana Wesleyan, Indiana Wesleyan University

 Source(s): https://in.linkedin.com/company/revobots

 Xavier University

 Quick answer: REVOBOTS has publicly discussed TASKBOT SCOUT/SCOUT XT activity at Xavier University in Cincinnati.

 The March 2026 SCOUT XT press release describes initial outdoor pilot validation supporting campus parking workflows,
 and a January 2026 release references early TASKBOT SCOUT deployments. Use the release’s stated chronology rather
 than asserting other unpublished rollout phases.

 ID: xavier | Terms: Xavier, Xavier campus

 Source(s): https://revobots.ai/scoutxt | https://revobots.ai/ces2026






REVOBOTS INC  |  Public Knowledge Base v1.0  |  REVIEW DRAFT                                                                                              6

PUBLIC EVENTS

 Arizona Robotics Innovation Month

 Quick answer: REVOBOTS publicly supported Arizona’s Robotics Innovation Month in April 2025.

 Its official announcement places the initiative in the wider Arizona robotics and innovation ecosystem. REVOBOTS is one
 participating organization, not the sole creator or sponsor of the statewide recognition.

 ID: azrobotics | Terms: Robotics Innovation Month, Arizona robotics

 Source(s): https://revobots.ai/robotics-innovation-month

 CES 2026

 Quick answer: REVOBOTS publicly announced a CES 2026 presence showcasing TASKBOT AVA and TASKBOT SCOUT.

 Its January 2026 release described its task-adaptive robotics positioning and participation with the City of Phoenix
 delegation at the Venetian Expo. Do not confuse CES 2026 with separately planned future CES appearances.

 ID: ces2026 | Terms: CES, Consumer Electronics Show, CES 2026

 Source(s): https://revobots.ai/ces2026

 Ellucian Live 2026

 Quick answer: REVOBOTS publicly reported showcasing TASKBOT SCOUT XT and previewing TASKBOT PORTER at
 Ellucian Live 2026.

 The company post described the higher-education operating context alongside Campus Innovation and referenced
 Xavier University campus experience. It also previewed PORTER as a multifunction mobile manipulation concept.

 ID: ellucian2026 | Terms: Ellucian Live, ELive26

 Source(s): https://www.linkedin.com/posts/revobots_ellucian-live-2026-recap-activity-7453099120279330816-ITgA

 Mobile World Congress Barcelona 2025

 Quick answer: REVOBOTS introduced TASKBOT internationally at Mobile World Congress Barcelona in March 2025.

 Company materials and an official REVOBOTS LinkedIn post identify MWC Barcelona (March 3–6, 2025) as a public
 showcase for TASKBOT, including a demonstration at PwC’s Connected Solutions booth.

 ID: mwc2025 | Terms: MWC25, MWC Barcelona, Mobile World Congress

 Source(s): https://revobots.ai/mwc25 | https://www.linkedin.com/posts/revobots_introducing-taskbot-activity-7302198556960993280-n6bs

 North American TASKBOT debut in Phoenix

 Quick answer: REVOBOTS announced a North American TASKBOT showcase at an AIVN event in Phoenix in April 2025.

 The press release places the April 17, 2025 introduction in Arizona’s Robotics Innovation Month and frames the event
 around human-guided, task-adaptive automation.

 ID: phoenix2025 | Terms: AIVN, Arizona Robotics Innovation Month, Phoenix debut

 Source(s): https://revobots.ai/aivn

 PwC EmTech Exchange 2026

 Quick answer: REVOBOTS shared an official public recap of its participation at PwC’s EmTech Exchange 2026.

 According to REVOBOTS’ LinkedIn recap, its TASKBOT demonstrations engaged enterprise audiences around physical AI
 and operational use cases. Keep this as an event participation statement, without extending it into unannounced future
 partnership commitments.





REVOBOTS INC  |  Public Knowledge Base v1.0  |  REVIEW DRAFT                                                                                         7

ID: emtech2026 | Terms: EmTech, EmTech Exchange

 Source(s): https://www.linkedin.com/posts/revobots_revobots-pwcs-emtechexchange-2026-activity-7440370244927455232-28hc |
 https://in.linkedin.com/company/revobots

 PwC — publicly disclosed appearances

 Quick answer: REVOBOTS has publicly described participating at PwC’s Connected Solutions MWC 2025 booth and PwC’s
 EmTech Exchange 2026.

 The public record supports specific event participation and demonstrations. It does not authorize disclosure of private
 agreement terms, internal meetings, unannounced work, or future engagements. Speak about the public events only.

 ID: pwc-public | Terms: PwC, PWC, EmTech PwC, PwC Connected Solutions

 Source(s): https://www.linkedin.com/posts/revobots_introducing-taskbot-activity-7302198556960993280-n6bs |
 https://www.linkedin.com/posts/revobots_revobots-pwcs-emtechexchange-2026-activity-7440370244927455232-28hc

 LEADERSHIP

 Andre Christian

 Quick answer: Andre Christian is a REVOBOTS co-founder responsible for executive brand, communications, and
 strategic positioning.

 The REVOBOTS press kit lists Andre Christian as co-founder and Chief Brand Officer, while its public site highlights his
 background in brand, growth, operations, and a former Toshiba director role. Company press releases quote him on the
 future of work, human-centered automation, and the benefits of purpose-built robotic systems. The current corporate
 executive title should be checked with approved external materials before precise role labels are refreshed; this profile
 intentionally avoids unpublished changes. Use the professional name Andre Christian.

 ID: founder-andre | Terms: André Christian, Andre, brand strategy, Chief Brand Officer

 Source(s): https://revobots.ai/press | https://revobots.ai/ | https://revobots.ai/ces2026

 Dr. Giby Raphael

 Quick answer: Dr. Giby Raphael is a REVOBOTS co-founder and Chief Executive Officer.

 REVOBOTS publicly presents Dr. Raphael as an executive with experience in robotics, AI, technology commercialization,
 and industry leadership. The corporate site identifies prior leadership in Intel robotics and IoT. An official REVOBOTS
 LinkedIn feature describes a Ph.D. in Robotics and Machine Learning from USC and an MBA from Cornell. At REVOBOTS,
 he communicates the task-adaptive, human-guided robotics vision and its real-world application. When responding to
 questions about his credentials or work, use the documented public material and avoid creating a more extensive
 biography than those sources support.

 ID: founder-giby | Terms: Giby, Giby Raphael, Dr. Raphael, CEO REVOBOTS

 Source(s): https://revobots.ai/press | https://revobots.ai/ | https://www.linkedin.com/posts/revobots_hitl-usc-cornell-activity-7302923347015737344-
 xAdj

 Dr. Rahul Khanna

 Quick answer: Dr. Rahul Khanna is a REVOBOTS co-founder and Chief AI Officer.

 The REVOBOTS press kit names Dr. Khanna as part of the founding leadership team, and the corporate website
 highlights his AI architecture expertise and patent portfolio. His public positioning includes intelligent systems,
 multimodal machine learning, and the intersection of AI with robotics. His leadership role focuses on the intelligence side
 of REVOBOTS’ task-adaptive platforms. Avoid inventing implementation details, confidential algorithms, or private R&D
 history.

 ID: founder-rahul | Terms: Rahul, Rahul Khanna, CAIO, Chief AI Officer





REVOBOTS INC  |  Public Knowledge Base v1.0  |  REVIEW DRAFT                                                                                               8

Source(s): https://revobots.ai/press | https://revobots.ai/ | https://www.linkedin.com/company/revobots/

 Dr. Ranjy Thomas

 Quick answer: Dr. Ranjy Thomas is a REVOBOTS co-founder and Chief Strategy Officer.

 REVOBOTS’ public press kit identifies Dr. Thomas as part of its founding team. The company website describes his
 background in entrepreneurship, executive strategy, enterprise advisory work, and strategic growth, including prior
 Nextel experience. He brings a market and organizational perspective to the company’s approach to introducing
 task-adaptive robotics into real operating environments. The public chatbot should not discuss private counterparties,
 future customer opportunities, or relationships that are not already announced.

 ID: founder-ranjy | Terms: Ranjy, Ranjy Thomas, CSO, Chief Strategy Officer

 Source(s): https://revobots.ai/press | https://revobots.ai/

 Mike Phillips

 Quick answer: Mike Phillips is a REVOBOTS co-founder and leads practical robotic design and manufacturing.

 The REVOBOTS press kit identifies Phillips as Chief Manufacturing & Design Officer. Official company LinkedIn
 descriptions emphasize his experience in robotic design, 3D printing, manufacturability, precision engineering, and the
 progression from prototype to working system. His contribution sits at the junction of mechanical feasibility, modular
 components, and real-world execution. Avoid unpublished build techniques, supplier details, and internal engineering
 problems.

 ID: founder-mike | Terms: Mike, Michael Phillips, Mike Phillips, CMDO, Chief Manufacturing & Design Officer

 Source(s): https://revobots.ai/press | https://revobots.ai/ | https://www.linkedin.com/company/revobots/

 FAQ

 Are all TASKBOTS humanoid?

 Quick answer: No. REVOBOTS develops task-adaptive robots in forms appropriate to the job; AVA is a humanoid-inspired
 platform while SCOUT is mobile.

 Earlier releases featured humanoid robotics prominently, while more recent communications emphasize that the
 task—not a fixed physical appearance—determines the solution. Different configurations are not interchangeable and
 must be assessed for the intended workflow.

 ID: faq-humanoid | Terms: humanoid versus task specific, do you make humanoids

 Source(s): https://revobots.ai/ces2026 | https://revobots.ai/ | https://revobots.ai/mwc25

 How are taskbots introduced into a new environment?

 Quick answer: REVOBOTS begins by understanding the workflow, environment, and desired task, then configures and
 validates the appropriate system.

 Public materials describe fast iteration, modular production, and human-in-the-loop oversight. Exact timelines,
 dependencies, acceptance criteria, and capabilities vary by use case and are established through direct discussions with
 REVOBOTS.

 ID: faq-deployment | Terms: how to deploy, start deployment, implementation

 Source(s): https://revobots.ai/ces2026 | https://revobots.ai/mwc25

 How can I learn more about REVOBOTS?

 Quick answer: Visit revobots.ai or contact REVOBOTS through its publicly listed press and corporate channels.







REVOBOTS INC  |  Public Knowledge Base v1.0  |  REVIEW DRAFT                                                                                              9

For product fit, demonstrations, or official statements, direct visitors to the corporate website. The company lists
 pr@revobots.ai for press inquiries in its public materials. Do not provide private founder contact details or personal
 addresses.

 ID: faq-contact | Terms: contact, media inquiries, request demo

 Source(s): https://revobots.ai/ | https://revobots.ai/press | https://revobots.ai/mwc25

 How do robots learn tasks?

 Quick answer: REVOBOTS describes combining AI-driven operation with human-in-the-loop instruction and oversight.

 Early-stage task guidance and remote operator support may help the system adapt to a workflow; subsequent robotic
 control is specific to the tested hardware and setting. Do not promise unrestricted learning or perfect performance.

 ID: faq-robot-learning | Terms: train a taskbot, robot teaching, how robots learn

 Source(s): https://revobots.ai/mwc25 | https://revobots.ai/aivn | https://revobots.ai/scoutxt

 How does REVOBOTS differ from traditional robotics?

 Quick answer: REVOBOTS starts with a defined task and adapts both robotic hardware and intelligence to that task.

 The public positioning emphasizes modular, 3D-printed components, tailored mobility and tooling, and human oversight
 when helpful. This allows the conversation to focus on work outcomes and deployment fit rather than the spectacle of a
 particular robot shape.

 ID: faq-difference | Terms: what makes revobots different, why revobots, differentiation

 Source(s): https://revobots.ai/ces2026 | https://revobots.ai/mwc25

 Questions outside approved knowledge

 Quick answer: I can share REVOBOTS’ published product and company information, but I do not have a verified public
 answer to that specific question.

 Offer to point the visitor to revobots.ai or invite a company representative to provide confirmed information. Never
 invent product availability, undisclosed customers, schedules, engineering specifications, leadership biographies,
 confidential arrangements, or current event commitments.

 ID: faq-known-unknown | Terms: I do not know, fallback, unknown answer

 Source(s): https://revobots.ai/

 What industries does REVOBOTS serve?

 Quick answer: REVOBOTS describes applications across campuses, logistics, manufacturing, retail, and service
 environments.

 Publicly evidenced campus operations are a particularly concrete example. Other sectors are discussed as targeted or
 potential applications; individual deployments should be named only where REVOBOTS has publicly announced them.

 ID: faq-industries | Terms: markets served, verticals, industries

 Source(s): https://revobots.ai/mwc25 | https://revobots.ai/ces2026 | https://revobots.ai/scoutxt

 EDITORIAL QUEUE: DO NOT LOAD INTO PUBLIC CHATBOT

 REVO BLADE — definition pending

 The permitted public sources reviewed did not establish what REVO BLADE refers to. No definition, specification,
 trademark status, or capability claim should be generated without Anup’s approved glossary or an official public source.







REVOBOTS INC  |  Public Knowledge Base v1.0  |  REVIEW DRAFT                                                                                          10

REVO 2-4-8 (editorial draft)

 User-authorized internal high-level description: roughly 2 days to clarify workflow and constraints, approximately 4
 weeks to present a working prototype or iteration, and approximately 8 weeks for further integration, validation, and
 deployment preparation. This has not yet been matched to an accessible public press release or approved glossary, and
 the milestone wording should be confirmed before public chatbot ingestion.

 TASKBOT RANGER — proposed public description

 The proposed description is limited to general concept-level context. The October 2026 project materials discuss a
 server/blade retrieval demonstration, but no independently accessible public product announcement was located in the
 permitted sources. Do not use this record in an external chatbot until the public description and launch status are
 approved.

 Data-center workflow concepts

 This topic comes from pre-public planning materials and should remain out of a public chatbot until a sanctioned
 announcement establishes the product, intended workflow, and status.

 CES 2027 status pending public release

 Do not disclose confidential planning, booth allocation, named future deliverables, or internal collaboration plans in the
 customer-facing knowledge base until an approved announcement or public content is supplied.

 MAINTENANCE AND INGESTION
